"The background check includes a United States criminal background check and a motor vehicle record (“MVR”) check. All checks will consider federal, state, and local regulations. • Criminal background check: This includes a review of convictions and pending matters in accordance with applicable law. Our approved vendor will search county, state, and federal criminal court sources of record. In accordance with applicable law, the check will include a review of 7 years of history from the date when the check is requested. ○ Nationwide Sex Offender Registry check: Search of the US Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Registry ○ Denied Party and Sanction: Global inter-governmental database search for restricted or sanctioned persons • Motor vehicle record check: This includes events, violations, and accidents listed on the driver’s license. "The timing of completion of the check will depend on a number of factors, including the driver's previous residential history, court turnaround times, and the driver's response to any requests for additional information. Checks take an average of 6 days, but may take longer. Drivers should continue to monitor their email while the background check is in progress, in case additional information is needed to complete the check to avoid unnecessary delays."

Drivers onboarding to Relay will initiate the background check process during account setup. Existing drivers should initiate the process from the Relay app when asked. In accordance with applicable law, Amazon may request additional checks throughout the time a driver hauls Relay loads.

To initiate the background check process, a driver must provide either an SSN or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN). Drivers will first be asked for their SSN. They can declare that they don’t have an SSN, and instead enter an ITIN. If a driver can’t provide either an SSN or ITIN, they can’t meet requirements for the check, and won’t be able to haul Relay loads.

They’ll be able to see a driver’s background check status (not started, past due, in review, email response required, meets requirements, requirements not met). Drivers who don’t meet the background check requirements won’t be able to haul Relay loads. Drivers can dispute the results of a background check directly with the company who completes the check. There may be a limit on how many times disputes can be filed.

If Electronic Braking System is not connected, the EBS OFF light will be lit when the engine is running.
How can a driver check that Electronic Braking System (EBS) is connected?

1. Connect your EBS! Remember to connect the Electronic Braking System (EBS) after coupling as this affects trailer ride height. 2. Know Your Height! Knowing the height of their equipment will help detect imminent danger and should be used as a last line of defense to prevent a low bridge strike. 3. Plan Ahead! Plan your route prior to departure to avoid low bridges. If you have to reroute, find a safe spot to stop and plan your new route. 4. Use the Relay Navigation System! We recommend using the Relay Mobile app which enables drivers to safely navigate trucks for Amazon Trips. The Relay Navigation System contained on the Relay Mobile app sets routes which factor in the specified dimensions of the vehicle and equipment type. The recommended routes are compliant with state/local regulations and with Amazon’s commitments to routes in residential areas. 5. Watch for Road Signs! While driving, always keep an eye out for road signs, particularly when approaching bridges.
How can a driver prevent a bridge strike?

Low clearance bridge strikes are a serious safety hazard, potentially resulting in injury and loss of life, damage to infrastructure, interruption of commerce, and delays in travel times. These accidents are preventable through better awareness of route restrictions along travel paths, gained by paying closer attention to road signs and by the use of only those electronic navigation systems intended for trucks and buses.
